The actual expression is, as far as the packet shows, a verbatim repetition of the frozen `corpus.text`. Its opening, its ten disagreements, and its final paragraph all match the source. So there is no translator-side loss between the frozen prose and the actual expression. The interesting losses and additions appear in the independent reading and in the two proposed languages, Lean WHL and RSS.

## The independent reading

The reading says: “Literally, it says that such a snapshot is not a single ledger but a bag of records—orderless, possibly duplicated, stale, or contradictory.” But the source distinguishes two levels:

> “A replicated warehouse snapshot is not a single ledger but a cloud of rival stories about what has been promised. The capacity and logical time are shared coordinates, but the records arrive as a bag…”

The snapshot is a cloud of rival stories; the records are a bag. The reading collapses the snapshot into the bag. That loses the source’s story/record distinction, which matters later when the source asks whether “true” means anything and whether alternatives are records or quantities.

The reading also treats the source as withheld. It says: “because the source corpus field is withheld, none of this establishes that the source language actually carried those categories,” and it says the “essayistic apparatus—‘first useful conjecture,’ ‘deliberate refusal,’ ‘Now the disagreements begin,’ ‘A conjecture,’ ‘A criticism,’ ‘keeping these disagreements visible’—is almost certainly carrier-side prose escape, not source content.” But the source is not withheld in this packet, and those phrases are in the frozen source itself. The defect is therefore in the probe or reader perspective, not in the expression. It is a source-text-withheld reading being applied where the source text is available.

There is an internal tension about expiry. The reading says the expression’s assumptions include “expiry as effect rather than deletion,” yet it also lists “whether expiry deletes or only zeroes” among what is left unresolved. The source is more precise:

> “The snapshot description tilts toward the first… So the first is better supported, but the second remains a live conjecture…”

The reading flattens that tilt into both an assumption and an open question. A proposed repair would be to preserve the source’s asymmetry: effect is better supported, deletion remains live.

The reading also introduces “a total order on revisions” as an assumption. The source only says higher revision supersedes lower revision. It does not state trichotomy, antisymmetry, or totality. That is an added formal commitment. Similarly, “descriptive or normative” and the meta-textual allegory reading are interpretive additions, not explicit source content. They may be admissible, but they should be marked as added.

## Lean WHL

The Lean sketch is declared as a language, not a translation, so its defects are in the carrier and compiler bridge. Several are concrete.

First, the code is not Lean-core-compatible as claimed. `Quantity` is an axiom, but `list_min?` and `list_max?` use `<` and `>` on `Quantity`. `availability_lower_bound` folds with `acc + booking_lower_bound snap b` starting from `0`, but `booking_lower_bound` returns `Quantity`, not `Nat`. `Int.sub_nat` expects `Nat`, but receives `Quantity`. `rules_disagree` uses `possible_reservations_with` before that definition appears. The inductive `Int` shadows Lean’s core `Int`. These are compiler-bridge defects. A repaired Lean could still encode more; the failure does not prove Lean cannot express the distinctions.

The semantic losses are more important. The source says:

> “Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing; authority does not accumulate by repetition.”

Lean defines `exact_duplicate`, but `possible_reservations` still maps every record at the greatest revision:

```lean
(rs.filter (λ r, r.booking = b ∧ greatest_revision_in rs r)).map (reserves_effect t)
```

If two exact duplicate active holds tie at the greatest revision, the resulting `List Quantity` can contain the same quantity twice. `list_min?` and `list_max?` ignore that for bounds, but the list itself can be read as multiple alternatives. The duplicate is not fully inert in the representation. A proposed repair would filter exact duplicates before mapping, or represent possible reservations as a set/quotient.

The source says:

> “Different records tied at a greatest revision can remain unresolved alternatives…”

But Lean’s `possible_reservations` maps records to `Quantity`. Two tied records with the same quantity but different expiry or kind collapse to the same quantity. The alternative is a record, not just a number. This loses the ability to criticize a particular record among tied alternatives. A proposed repair would preserve record identity, perhaps returning `List Record` or a set of records plus their effects.

The largest Lean defect is expiry. The source says:

> “Another reading treats expiry as deleting the record from the bag, after which revision 3 becomes greatest and active, so the booking reserves again.”

Lean defines `expired_deletes_rule`, but it is identical to `reserves_effect`: an expired hold maps to zero, and a release maps to zero. `possible_reservations_with` still uses `greatest_revision_in rs r` on the original list. So revision 5 remains greatest; revision 3 never becomes greatest. The “deletion” reading is named but not implemented. A proposed repair would make a reading transform the snapshot or the greatest-revision relation before computing reservations.

The source also says:

> “One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking’s history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful.”

Lean defines `Conjecture : Type := Snapshot → Prop` and `Refutation` only over `Conjecture`. Rule criticism is not directly a `Conjecture`; `rules_disagree` is only a `Prop`. This narrows what criticism can target. A proposed repair would parameterize conjectures over a target type, or define separate conjecture/refutation structures for rules, records, bookings, and assumptions.

Lean admits it does not model source-assumption dependence, replication, per-replica logical time, or physical resource sharing beyond capacity. Those admissions are honest, but they are still lost distinctions. In particular, the source warns:

> “intervals lose correlations: booking A’s high alternative might be incompatible with booking B’s high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot.”

Lean’s `availability_lower_bound` and `availability_upper_bound` sum independent per-booking minima and maxima. That can produce an interval wider than any actually possible combination. The language notes the limitation, but it cannot express the correlation.

## RSS

RSS adds a richer ontology: Story, Bag, Coordinate, Viewpoint, Conflict, Liveness, Reading, Projection, Account, Inquiry State. This is not wrong as a proposed language, but it is not neutral. It says:

> “A story is not a record. Records are evidence for stories.”

The source says the snapshot is a “cloud of rival stories,” but it also says “the records arrive as a bag.” It does not say records are evidence for stories. RSS introduces a layer between records and stories. That may be useful, but it changes the base object of the reconstruction.

RSS also changes exact duplication. The source says duplicates are the same in booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry. RSS says:

> “Exact duplication: two deliveries are exact duplicates if all record fields and provenance are equal.”

Adding provenance to duplicate identity means two deliveries with the same five source fields but different provenance are not exact duplicates under RSS. That contradicts the source’s five-field rule. A proposed repair would keep exact duplication on the five fields and treat provenance separately.

RSS treats coordinates as viewpoint-relative:

> “RSS treats coordinates as parameters of a viewpoint, not as absolute facts.”

The source says capacity and logical time are “shared coordinates.” It later allows that different replicas may have different logical times, so a viewpoint-relative treatment is a possible reading. But RSS makes it the default, losing the shared-coordinate baseline.

RSS also flattens the source’s tilt on expiry. The source says the first reading is “better supported,” while the second “remains a live conjecture.” RSS says:

> “RSS does not choose a reading. It compares readings.”

That preserves coexistence but loses the support relation. A proposed repair would add a relation of evidential support between readings, not only a set of readings.

RSS adds that deliveries may differ in logical time. The source says different replicas may have different logical times; it does not say deliveries carry logical time. That is an added commitment. RSS also has an internal inconsistency: it makes provenance a primitive, then says in its limitations that “RSS cannot express the exact provenance of a delivery unless provenance is added.” A proposed repair would remove one side of that contradiction.

To RSS’s credit, it preserves more of the source’s disagreement structure than Lean does. It distinguishes exact and near duplicates, represents multiple readings of expiry and release, allows criticism to target records, rules, bookings, snapshots, coordinates, or assumptions, and carries negative availability as a signal rather than an error. Its noncomputability also honestly reflects the source’s refusal to force a single answer, though it may obstruct the source’s “natural reconstruction” procedure.

## Disposition

The actual expression is faithful to the frozen source. The independent reading is partly misdirected by its source-withheld stance and collapses the story/record distinction. Lean WHL has concrete compiler-bridge errors and semantic gaps around duplicate inertness, record identity, expiry deletion, and criticism targets. RSS introduces an added ontology and misaligns exact duplication with provenance, but it preserves more of the source’s pluralism.

These are proposed repairs only; the source and languages remain frozen. The meta-textual allegory reading remains a competing interpretation. The expiry-deletion reading remains live but less supported. Neither Lean nor RSS is an obligatory grammar for the prose. A substantive prose objection remains admissible even where a selected formal language cannot encode it—for example, that tied alternatives are records, not merely quantities, and that a duplicate delivery must not become a second alternative merely because it appears twice in a list.

history.text:
A replicated warehouse snapshot is not a single ledger but a cloud of rival stories about what has been promised. The capacity and logical time are shared coordinates, but the records arrive as a bag: orderless, possibly repeated, possibly stale, possibly contradictory. The first useful conjecture is that the snapshot's job is not to compute one timeless answer but to decide which conflicts are still alive. Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing; authority does not accumulate by repetition. A higher revision kills lower revisions for that booking, but only within the booking. Two bookings can disagree about which revision they have accepted without infecting each other.

For any one booking, the natural reconstruction is to group its records by revision, then keep only the greatest revision present. Within that greatest revision, a hold and a release cannot both be in force as the same fact; they are alternatives. An expired hold and a release both reserve zero. An active hold reserves its quantity. If several active holds tie at the greatest revision, they remain unresolved alternatives, not a sum and not a vote. That is a deliberate refusal: the rules do not say how to merge them, so the snapshot should retain the possibility that any one is the true one, or that none is, depending on what "true" is taken to mean.

Availability is then capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected, but the word "actually" hides the problem. If each booking's greatest revision is unambiguous, availability may still be negative if the selected holds exceed capacity. Negative availability is not an error in the arithmetic; it is a signal that the warehouse has over-promised relative to this reconstruction. If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one. A pessimistic reading takes the maximum hold among alternatives for each booking; an optimistic reading takes the minimum. Neither is forced by the snapshot alone.

Now the disagreements begin.

One disagreement is whether uncertainty should be retained at all. A reconciler might collapse each tie to the largest quantity, or to the earliest expiry, or to the record with some lexical tiebreak, and thereby produce a single availability number. That is convenient, but it manufactures authority. Another reconciler might keep all alternatives and report a range. That preserves honesty but makes downstream decisions harder. The snapshot description does not settle which is correct; it only says tied records can remain unresolved. A conjecture: the more useful representation is a partial order of possible reservations, not a set, because some alternatives may be compatible with others across bookings while others are not. A criticism: once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain.

A second disagreement concerns expiry and obsolete records. If logical current time is past a hold's expiry, that hold reserves zero. But does expiry erase the record, demote it, or merely change its effect? Suppose a booking has revision 5 expired and revision 3 active. Higher revision supersedes lower revision, so revision 5 wins, and because it is expired it reserves zero. Revision 3 is obsolete and should not be resurrected. That reading treats revision as authority and expiry as effect. Another reading treats expiry as deleting the record from the bag, after which revision 3 becomes greatest and active, so the booking reserves again. These give opposite answers. The snapshot description tilts toward the first: a higher revision supersedes lower revisions, and expiry can make a hold reserve zero. It does not say expiry removes the supersession. So the first is better supported, but the second remains a live conjecture, especially if one thinks expired records are no longer "delivered records" in the relevant sense. A criticism of the first: it lets a dead revision keep a live one buried forever, which may be undesirable operationally.

A third disagreement is what a criticism targets. One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful. For example, saying "this snapshot is inconsistent" might mean two active holds for one booking at the same greatest revision, or it might mean total reservations exceed capacity, or it might mean the logical time is behind an expiry that someone expected to have passed. These are different claims. A conjecture: many apparent disagreements about availability are really disagreements about which target a criticism addresses. A criticism of the rule "higher revision always supersedes" is not the same as a criticism of a record that carries a high revision but an implausible quantity. Preserving that distinction matters because one can reject a rule while accepting the data, or accept the rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late.

A fourth disagreement concerns source assumptions. The snapshot assumes records are delivered, but not that they are complete. It assumes duplicates convey no additional authority, but not that all duplicates are identical in every field; if two records share booking and revision but differ in kind or quantity, are they duplicates or alternatives? The description says duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority, which suggests exact duplicates are inert, but near-duplicates may be unresolved alternatives. It assumes logical current time is a single coordinate, but different replicas may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative. It assumes bookings are independent, but capacity is shared, so reservations interact. It assumes a release or expired hold reserves zero, but does not say whether a release at a lower revision can cancel a hold at a higher revision. By the supersession rule, no: the higher hold wins. By a cancellation rule, maybe yes. That is a source assumption about what "release" means.

A fifth disagreement is whether availability should be computed per booking or globally. Per booking, one can say each booking's reservation is the quantity of its greatest-revision active hold, or zero otherwise, or unresolved among tied greatest-revision active holds. Globally, availability is capacity minus the sum. But if there are unresolved alternatives, the sum is not well-defined. One can compute a lower bound by taking the minimum reservation per booking and an upper bound by taking the maximum. That gives an interval, but intervals lose correlations: booking A's high alternative might be incompatible with booking B's high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot. The snapshot does not name physical resources, so this incompatibility is invisible. A conjecture: the snapshot is under-specified for any real warehouse, and the best one can do is expose the unresolved alternatives rather than pretend to a single answer. A criticism: exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently.

A sixth disagreement concerns negative availability. If capacity is 10 and active holds sum to 12, availability is -2. Some might call this an inconsistency and reject the snapshot. Others might call it a valid state of over-reservation. The description says availability can be negative, which suggests over-reservation is allowed. But negative availability does not say which holds are the offenders. If there are alternatives, some combinations may be negative and others not. A conjecture: the sign of availability is less important than the set of reservations that produce it, because a negative number alone does not tell you which booking to revisit. A criticism: if availability is allowed to be negative, then capacity is not a hard constraint, and the word "capacity" may be misleading; it is more like a soft target or a reporting threshold.

A seventh disagreement is about revision gaps and missing records. Suppose a booking has revision 7 and revision 5, but no revision 6. Does revision 7 supersede revision 5? Yes, if higher revision supersedes lower. Does the absence of revision 6 matter? Not by the stated rules, but it might indicate a lost delivery. A conjecture: revision numbers are not necessarily contiguous, and treating a gap as evidence of loss is an extra assumption. A criticism: if revisions are generated in order, a gap may be meaningful, and ignoring it may hide a delivery failure.

An eighth disagreement is about tie-breaking across bookings. Different bookings need not share the same choice, so one cannot impose a global tiebreak. But a downstream consumer might want a single availability number. To get one, it must choose per booking, possibly arbitrarily. That choice is not authorized by the snapshot. A conjecture: any single-number availability is a projection that discards information, and different projections can disagree even when they respect the snapshot. A criticism: without a projection, the snapshot cannot answer the simple question "how much is available?" That may be acceptable if the snapshot's role is to support inquiry rather than to issue verdicts.

A ninth disagreement is about time. Logical current time is given, but records have expiries. If logical time advances, expired holds become zero. Does an expired hold at a high revision still supersede a lower active hold? As above, one reading says yes. Another says expiry is a state change that makes the high revision inactive, allowing a lower revision to become relevant if it is still active. The description does not resolve this. A conjecture: the safer reading is that supersession is structural and expiry is evaluative; the high revision remains the chosen record, but its contribution is zero. A criticism: this can leave a booking with no reservation even though an older active hold exists, which may violate an operator's expectation that the warehouse still holds the goods.

A tenth disagreement is about what "delivered" means. A record delivered to one replica may not be delivered to another. The snapshot is described as replicated, but the bag is unordered. Does the snapshot represent the union of all deliveries, or the intersection, or one replica's view? If it is a union, it may contain alternatives that no single replica has. If it is an intersection, it may omit records that matter. A conjecture: the snapshot is a merge, and merging is itself a source of uncertainty, because different replicas may have different logical times and different sets of records. A criticism: the description treats the snapshot as a single object, which may obscure the replication problem rather than solve it.

Finally, there is the question of what remains material for inquiry. False or incomplete proposals are not discarded; they are part of the evidence about how people understand the system. A conjecture that a release always cancels a hold, even across revisions, may be false under the stated supersession rule, but it reveals an assumption about what releases are for. A conjecture that ties should be summed may be false under the "unresolved alternatives" reading, but it reveals a desire for conservatism. A criticism that the snapshot is unusable because it does not resolve ties may be substantive, but it may also be a demand for a decision that the snapshot was never meant to make. Keeping these disagreements visible is not a failure of the reconstruction; it is the reconstruction's only honest form.

The expression is not one proposition but an essayistic reconstruction. It presents a model of a replicated warehouse snapshot, then uses that model to stage a series of interpretive disagreements. Literally, it says that such a snapshot is not a single ledger but a bag of records—orderless, possibly duplicated, stale, or contradictory. The records carry a booking, a revision, a kind, a quantity, and an expiry. Capacity and logical time are shared coordinates. Exact duplicate delivery adds no authority. Within one booking, a higher revision supersedes lower revisions. For a booking, one groups by revision and keeps the greatest revision present; within that revision, a hold and a release are alternatives rather than two facts that can both be in force. An expired hold and a release both reserve zero; an active hold reserves its quantity. If several active holds tie at the greatest revision, they remain unresolved alternatives, not a sum and not a vote. Availability is then capacity minus whatever reservation is “actually” selected, but that word hides the problem: if alternatives remain, availability is not a number but a set, an interval, or possibly a non-convex range. A pessimistic reading takes the maximum hold among alternatives; an optimistic reading takes the minimum. Neither is forced by the snapshot alone.

The essay then turns to ten disagreements: whether to retain uncertainty or collapse ties; whether expiry merely zeroes a record or deletes it so an older active revision revives; what a criticism targets—rule, record, booking history, snapshot, or logical time; what source assumptions are in play about delivered records, completeness, duplicate identity, replica-relative time, booking independence, and release semantics; whether availability is per booking or global; whether negative availability is an error or a valid over-reservation; whether revision gaps matter; whether cross-booking tie-breaking is ever authorized; how expiry interacts with supersession; and what “delivered” means when replicas may differ. The final methodological claim is that false or incomplete proposals are still evidence, and that keeping disagreements visible is not a failure of reconstruction but the reconstruction’s only honest form.

There is also a strong competing reading: the warehouse snapshot may be an allegory for interpreting a source corpus itself. On that reading, records are source fragments, bookings are topics or concepts, revisions are candidate versions, holds and releases are assertions and retractions, expiry is obsolescence, capacity is coherence or consistency, logical time is context, and availability is what can be concluded. The final paragraph—about false or incomplete proposals as evidence and disagreements as the honest form of reconstruction—supports this meta-textual reading. So the expression can be read literally as a data-model essay or rhetorically as a commentary on translation, reconstruction, and the refusal to force a single answer. Which reading is primary is itself left unresolved.

What it leaves unresolved is extensive: whether the rules are descriptive or normative; whether the snapshot is one replica’s view, an intersection, or a union; whether expiry deletes or only zeroes; whether a lower-revision release can cancel a higher-revision hold; whether near-duplicates are alternatives or inert; whether revision gaps indicate loss; how ties should be resolved, if at all; whether availability must be global or per booking; whether intervals lose invisible correlations across bookings; whether negative availability is allowed or pathological; whether capacity is a hard constraint or a soft target; and how “true,” “actually,” and “delivered” are to be understood. The expression does not settle these; it deliberately keeps them open.

Its assumptions include bag semantics for records; a total order on revisions; supersession as authority within a booking; booking independence for supersession even though capacity is shared; exact duplicate inertness; hold and release as mutually exclusive alternatives at the same revision; expiry as effect rather than deletion; active hold as quantity; logical current time as a single shared coordinate; availability as capacity minus selected reservations; and the legitimacy of representing unresolved alternatives as sets, intervals, or partial orders. It also assumes that the snapshot can be treated as a single object despite being replicated, and that the source description does not specify a tie-breaking policy.

Criticisms are both acknowledged and invited. Collapsing ties manufactures authority. Keeping alternatives pushes the problem downstream. Moving to possible worlds smuggles in a notion of possibility the original bag may not have contained. Treating expiry as mere effect lets a dead revision bury a live one. Allowing negative availability makes “capacity” sound like a hard constraint when it may be a soft target. Single-number availability is an arbitrary projection that discards information. Treating the snapshot as a single object obscures replication. Exposing alternatives without a resolution policy may be unusable. The essay may also overinterpret the source by adding categories—conjecture, criticism, possible worlds, partial order, convexity—that the source may not have carried. And its final preference for visible disagreement is itself a normative stance, not a neutral description.

Visible source-like quotations or embedded translations are mostly terms and rule summaries: “true,” “actually,” “delivered records,” “release,” “capacity,” “inconsistent,” and “how much is available?” are marked as quoted or problematic words. The repeated “The description says…” phrases—duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority; higher revision supersedes lower revisions; expiry can make a hold reserve zero; tied records can remain unresolved; availability can be negative—appear to summarize source rules. But because the source corpus field is withheld, none of this establishes that the source language actually carried those categories. The expression is therefore best treated as a mediated interpretation that may preserve some source vocabulary while adding a great deal of its own structure.

That preserves coexistence but loses the support relation. A proposed repair would add a relation of evidential support between readings, not only a set of readings.

RSS adds that deliveries may differ in logical time. The source says different replicas may have different logical times; it does not say deliveries carry logical time. That is an added commitment. RSS also has an internal inconsistency: it makes provenance a primitive, then says in its limitations that “RSS cannot express the exact provenance of a delivery unless provenance is added.” A proposed repair would remove one side of that contradiction.

To RSS’s credit, it preserves more of the source’s disagreement structure than Lean does. It distinguishes exact and near duplicates, represents multiple readings of expiry and release, allows criticism to target records, rules, bookings, snapshots, coordinates, or assumptions, and carries negative availability as a signal rather than an error. Its noncomputability also honestly reflects the source’s refusal to force a single answer, though it may obstruct the source’s “natural reconstruction” procedure.

## Disposition

The actual expression is faithful to the frozen source. The independent reading is partly misdirected by its source-withheld stance and collapses the story/record distinction. Lean WHL has concrete compiler-bridge errors and semantic gaps around duplicate inertness, record identity, expiry deletion, and criticism targets. RSS introduces an added ontology and misaligns exact duplication with provenance, but it preserves more of the source’s pluralism.

These are proposed repairs only; the source and languages remain frozen. The meta-textual allegory reading remains a competing interpretation. The expiry-deletion reading remains live but less supported. Neither Lean nor RSS is an obligatory grammar for the prose. A substantive prose objection remains admissible even where a selected formal language cannot encode it—for example, that tied alternatives are records, not merely quantities, and that a duplicate delivery must not become a second alternative merely because it appears twice in a list.
